correctness.rationale: All commuting idempotents yield orthogonal spectral idempotents; explicit g=sum f_gamma d_gamma in 1+J conjugates the canonical tuple. The stabilizer is the equal-color Peirce radical, yielding exact orbit q-power cardinality; left/right rank follows from right/left ideals; dual-number tangent conjugation proves geometric smoothness and component dimensions. The multigraph Potts identity and reverse polynomial reconstruction are algebraically derived. Ten direct prime-field enumerations over actual multiplication tables independently match the coefficient formula.

The possibility that a general lifting/counting framework makes it a routine corollary is recorded as residual risk, not assumed disproved. The arbitrary-arity incidence coloring census may be implied by polynomial-potent matrix counts via a distinct-spectrum encoding; its apparent lack of explicit tuple wording does not establish novelty. The claim is not limited to incidence algebras.

evidence: Classical radical conjugacy makes each coloring a single 1+J orbit; routine orbit-stabilizer then gives q-power sizes. Known incidence single-idempotent statements are special cases. claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior orbit and special-case results imply substantial pieces, which are acknowledged. A more general equivalence theorem not found would be decisive coverage; residual risk remains.

originality.rationale: The assessed contribution combines an exact all-arity and all-field labeled bi-regular-rank census for arbitrary split basic algebras, algebraic-component data, and a reversible characterization of the total tuple counts by a random-cluster polynomial. The general conjugacy/lifting principle and previously enumerated single-idempotent incidence special cases are explicitly credited, not presented as novel. Public full-text results inspected do not state this all-arity enriched combination, though classical generalizations and unstated implications remain a genuine priority risk.
residual_risks: Classical simultaneous idempotent lifting and conjugation combined with a standard orbit-stabilizer argument may imply much of the orbit census; a stronger unstated all-arity corollary could subsume the formula.
Some full articles, notably the entire Mazurek–Nielsen–Ziembowski paper, were not inspected in full; no whole-paper not-covering inference is made.
More broadly, general Hall-polynomial, finite monoid or representation-count results might encode the complete weighted census or Potts inverse without identical terminology.
No independent historical-priority or expert mathematical audit has been performed.

Fixed-diagonal polynomial-potent incidence counts can encode multiple commuting idempotents in sufficiently large fields, possibly subsuming the incidence instance and its special rank information via interpolation.

value.rationale: A natural and complete multivariate invariant across all finite-dimensional split basic algebras and arbitrary finite fields, not an unmotivated finite instance. Its reversible relation to a random-cluster polynomial explains exactly what unrefined counts encode; orientation-sensitive bi-ranks detect another layer, while a path/radical-square-zero example proves a precise information-loss boundary. These distinctions are structurally meaningful for radical Peirce data and module dimensions.
